spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Two apparently different expansions are made comparable by decomposing each into independent blocks. Markings record which partition blocks are paired and reduction forgets the marks while retaining the resulting partition; on the determinant side, disjoint permutation cycles become independent Fourier factors. The mathematical work is the discovery of a shared set-partition skeleton beneath Möbius coefficients and determinant cycles.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For a marked partition (G,phi), reduction joins each paired positive/negative block and leaves unmarked blocks alone. Regrouping the sum of mu(O,G) C_G by the reduced partition F makes its coefficient factor over the blocks F_j, producing the X_{F_j} factors of Proposition 4.1. Separately, expanding W_n over permutations and decomposing a permutation into disjoint cycles makes its Fourier transform factor cyclewise. For one cycle, a change to successive differences and Parseval give a zero-sum delta times an integral of shifted copies of f_2; regrouping cycles by their supports yields Proposition 4.2.
directed.conceptual_reading: The proof aligns two global expressions by exposing their irreducible combinatorial components. Marking is an information-rich representation of pair formation, while reduction deliberately forgets the marks after they have supplied the correct local weight. Cycle decomposition performs the analogous localization for the determinant. Once both sides are multiplicative over partition blocks, the remaining comparison can be made one block at a time.

Parseval converts the cyclic kernel convolution into the overlap representation.

unit_result_entry.why_material: Square-integrable p-adic representations are built from supercuspidals, Rankin-Selberg factors vanish outside matching twist classes, and regrouping matched blocks into explicit positive-factor products locates the first pole and bounds local Langlands parameters below one half.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Langlands quotients organize general local factors
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: A non-tempered generic local representation is decomposed into tempered blocks with ordered real parameters, tempered blocks into square-integrable constituents, and principal L-factors multiply along both stages.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Local factorization yields nonnegative Rankin-Selberg coefficients
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Taking logarithms of the twist-class product writes each relevant coefficient as sums of squared magnitudes, giving a lower bound that implies nonnegativity of the global Rankin-Selberg Dirichlet coefficients.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Twist equivalence sparsifies the self Rankin-Selberg product: constituents in different twist classes do not interact, while each surviving class becomes an explicit positive-looking Euler product. That block factorization exposes the first pole as an extremal detector for the real Langlands parameters, converting local classification into the half-bound used earlier in the paper.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: A p-adic square-integrable representation is written as Delta(n,rho), built from twists of a unitary supercuspidal rho, and its principal factor reduces to that of rho with a shift. Rankin-Selberg factors between supercuspidals vanish unless the constituents are appropriately twist-equivalent; the Delta-by-Delta formula then reduces general factors to these cases. Decomposing a Langlands quotient into Delta(n_j,rho_j) blocks and partitioning the rho_j into twist classes factors L(s,pi_p x pi_p-dual) classwise. Unitarity rewrites each class as an explicit product in z_j and conjugate z_k. Its first pole is at twice the largest absolute real Langlands parameter; cited holomorphy for Re s>=1 therefore gives max |t_j|<1/2 and the corresponding principal-parameter bound.
directed.conceptual_reading: The twist-class partition is a structural sparsity device: it discards zero interactions and confines all pole-producing terms to equivalence blocks. Reparameterizing by z_j makes unitarity visible as conjugate pairing. Pole location then reads off the largest hidden growth parameter, so analytic regularity constrains each local constituent.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge objects are the atomic Delta(n,rho) representations, twist classes of supercuspidals, their class factors L_{F_l}, the variables z_j encoding length and shift, and the first pole of the resulting Euler product. They connect local representation classification to bounds on Satake or Langlands parameters.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The half-bound uses an external local-holomorphy result and the generic unitary hypotheses; factorization alone does not supply it. This span proves only the strict one-half threshold, not the later global improvement. Claims about exact poles and factors depend on the displayed indices and shifts.
directed.uncertainty: The classwise factorization and pole argument are well supported by prose. Numerous exponents, conjugations, divisibility parameters, and product bounds are extraction-sensitive and require the retained PDF for exact quotation.

supported: The construction of square-integrable p-adic blocks from supercuspidals, the Delta-by-Delta factor formula, partition into twist classes, classwise Euler product, unitarity symmetry, first-pole location, and strict half-bound are all supported by the span.
The candidate correctly records that the half-bound uses the cited holomorphy of the local Rankin-Selberg factor and does not arise from factorization alone.
The bridge from twist classes and z variables to Langlands-parameter and principal-root bounds is source-grounded.
inference: Describing twist classes as a sparsity device and pole location as an extremal detector is a useful inference from the factors that become trivial and the stated first-pole calculation.
unsupported_or_imported: The directed analysis says Rankin-Selberg factors between off-class supercuspidals 'vanish'; the source says the local factor equals 1 unless the representations are appropriately twist-equivalent. A local L-factor being trivial is not the same as vanishing.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: 'Positive-looking Euler product' is premature and imprecise here; coefficient positivity is established only in the next unit by taking logarithms and exposing sums of squares.
context_or_ocr_risk: The displayed shifts, conjugations, divisibility parameter, and product ranges are extraction-sensitive, so exact formulas and pole multiplicities require scan verification.
missed_mechanism: The no-interaction statement should be expressed as triviality of off-class factors, preserving the multiplicative identity element.
revision_instructions: Replace 'factors ... vanish' with 'factors are trivial (equal to 1)' outside the matching twist class, and describe (5.12) as an explicit classwise Euler product without suggesting positivity before the subsequent sum-of-squares argument.

unit_result_entry.why_material: Nonnegative Rankin-Selberg coefficients plus meromorphic continuation let Landau's theorem bound coefficient growth; taking high powers isolates each local parameter and yields the exponent 1/2 minus 1/(m^2+1), with an analogous spherical archimedean estimate cited.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Archimedean factor classification and a global proof of the half-bound
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Real Langlands quotients reduce to characters and discrete series, whose gamma factors give the completed local term; comparing the first local pole with global Rankin-Selberg holomorphy proves the archimedean parameter half-bound and avoids a more complicated local classification proof.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Local representation structure makes Rankin-Selberg coefficients positive and locates local poles, while global continuation, holomorphy, and Landau estimates feed back to sharpen local parameter bounds used in the global prime-sum analysis.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Several exact local formulas are text-layer fragile, and the strongest archimedean improvement stated at the end is cited for the spherical case rather than derived there.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Local-global feedback loop for analytic control

warnings: PDF extraction may degrade formulas, ligatures, or reading order; original retained

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Global positivity is fed back into every local place. Landau's theorem bounds nonnegative Rankin-Selberg coefficients; evaluating those bounds on arbitrarily high prime powers amplifies the largest local parameter until it can no longer hide among the others. The same mechanism reaches ramified places through the earlier twist-class square lower bound, producing a uniform improved exponent.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For the global self Rankin-Selberg series, nonnegative coefficients plus its meromorphic continuation, Gamma-factor degree data, and poles at zero and one allow Landau's theorem to give a summatory asymptotic and a pointwise coefficient bound. At an unramified prime, the relation between b(p^e) and the squared power sum of the local parameters bounds those sums for every e; passing through high powers yields |alpha_pi(p,j)|<=p^{1/2-1/(m^2+1)}. At ramified primes, Lemma 5.1 supplies the needed square lower bounds along multiples of r_l, giving the same control on the real Langlands parameters and hence on the principal local roots. A matching-looking spherical archimedean estimate is cited from another method.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is a local-global feedback loop. Positivity lets a global average theorem become pointwise coefficient control, and prime-power amplification converts coefficient growth into a spectral-radius bound on each local parameter. The ramified argument works because the twist-class representation retained a noncancelling square certificate.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is global Dirichlet coefficients b(n), their Landau growth bound, prime-power coefficients b(p^e), power sums of unramified local roots or squared twist-class sums at ramified primes, and finally the local Langlands parameters in the principal factor.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The conclusion depends on the stated analytic continuation, Gamma-factor data, pole structure, and coefficient positivity. The infinity statement is only cited, is restricted here to spherical pi_infinity, and is not established by the displayed finite-place proof. The extracted typography of the exponent is damaged.
directed.uncertainty: The argument supports the exponent 1/2-1/(m^2+1) through both finite-place cases, but its displayed fractions and epsilon exponents should be checked in the retained PDF. The archimedean analogue has citation rather than proof status in this span.

supported: For finite places, the candidate accurately follows positivity plus meromorphic continuation and Gamma-degree data through Landau's summatory estimate to a pointwise coefficient bound.
It correctly separates the unramified prime-power power-sum argument from the ramified twist-class square lower bound and obtains the same exponent for the finite local roots.
The directed analysis and boundary correctly state that the spherical archimedean estimate is cited from a different method rather than proved by the displayed finite-place argument.
inference: 'Prime-power amplification' and 'spectral-radius bound' are reasonable interpretations of passing to arbitrarily high powers to isolate the largest local modulus.
unsupported_or_imported: The spontaneous claim that global positivity is fed back into 'every local place' overgeneralizes the mechanism: this proof establishes the feedback at finite places, while the infinity estimate is only cited, is spherical, and explicitly comes from a quite different method.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: 'Matching-looking' is vague, but the directed and boundary fields supply the exact restriction and citation status.
context_or_ocr_risk: The extracted fraction typography and epsilon exponents are broken across lines; the prose and surrounding formulas support the stated finite exponent, but literal transcription should be scan-checked.
missed_mechanism: The opening conceptual summary should distinguish the proved all-finite-place feedback loop from the separately cited spherical archimedean analogue.
revision_instructions: Change 'every local place' to 'every finite place' and explicitly keep the infinity statement outside this Landau/twist-class mechanism as a cited spherical result obtained by another method.
